_about: Where a portal may be placed, and how big it is. The remake's portals.json has a
'placement' block and marks it _guess, saying so outright: its _radius_note reads
'Binary has g_portalCollisionRadius / portalCollisionRadius; value unknown.' These
are the decoded answers, and they replace that block's radius the way transit.json
'What the decode leaves for later steps'.
TWO radii, not one. The port carried a single collision_radius_px and used it for
both a placed portal's own trigger and the circle in which an antiportal refuses a
tap. They are unrelated: the first is a constant, the second is half the field

_source: Portal.angelscript, bytes 297250..297291: g_portalCollisionRadius = 14. The
PortalManager's constructor stores getScale() * 14 (bytes 297250.., instruction
111-113), and one scale unit is one of the port's pixels - preLoop calls
updateScaleFactor(256) and the port's view is 256 px tall - so it is 14 of them.
This is the circle a traveller enters a placed portal by. It is NOT what refuses
a tap near an antiportal.
PortalManager's constructor sets FIRST_PORTAL_MIN_TIME = 300 and
NEXT_PORTAL_MIN_TIME = 400 (bytes 137xxx, instructions 134-140). The remake's
portals.json carries 0.0 s and 0.25 s and admits them: 'The names are real; the
numbers are invented.' These are the real ones, in milliseconds.
THEY GATE TWO DIFFERENT THINGS.
first_ms gates the whole tap-reading path. PortalManager::update (bytes
138545..139692) jumps past managePortalInsertion when the game is paused, or
finished, or gameTimer.getTime() < FIRST_PORTAL_MIN_TIME. Both timers are
built in the PortalManager's constructor and a manager is built per level, so
this is 300 ms from the START OF EVERY LEVEL, not once per session.
next_ms gates ONE TAP, inside managePortalInsertion (bytes 143178..144166),
after hasPortalRequestInput and the touch position: the tap proceeds only when
lastPortalTimer.getTime() > NEXT_PORTAL_MIN_TIME.
RESET ON ACCEPTANCE, NOT ON SUCCESS. Timer::reset on lastPortalTimer runs at
instruction 78, BEFORE SeekEntity('projectile.ent') and before
computePortalFinalPos reports hasFailed. So a shot that flies off and opens
nothing still spends the 400 ms.
That does not contradict the owner's 'a failed shot costs nothing' (11
September): that is about the portal BUDGET, which a failed shot does not spend
and the port already gets right. The firing rate is a separate thing, and the
script is unambiguous about it. Do not make one match the other.
_both_start_at_zero: Timer's constructor calls its own reset (Timer.angelscript, bytes
38787..38883 and 39242..39299), update adds getLastFrameElapsedTime, and a
PortalManager - with both Timers - is built per level. So gameTimer and
lastPortalTimer are BOTH at zero when a level begins, and the first tap of a
level is held off by the LARGER of the two: 400 ms, not 300. That is the
original's behaviour, not an artefact of this port.
The comparisons differ and the port copies each: update refuses while gameTimer
is BELOW first_ms, managePortalInsertion proceeds only when lastPortalTimer is
ABOVE next_ms - so it refuses on equal.

_source: isPointInAntiPortalField (AntiPortalManager.angelscript, bytes 334800..335020):
r = entity.GetSize().x * 0.5
return squaredDistance(entity.GetPositionXY(), p) < r * r
so the radius is half the FIELD ENTITY'S OWN SIZE, not a constant. Followed into
the Ethanon source, which the remake's own rules call the only trustworthy spec:
- the script's GetSize binds to ETHScriptEntity::GetCurrentSize
(ETHScriptObjRegister.generic.cpp:222 and :358). There is no GetSize member;
- ETHSpriteEntity::GetCurrentSize (ETHSpriteEntity.cpp:652) returns
m_pSprite->GetFrameSize() * m_properties.scale;
- antiportal.ent draws white_ring.png with SpriteCut 1x1, and that image is
128 x 128 - so the frame is the whole of it;
- SGlobalScale::scaleEntity multiplies m_properties.scale by the node's own
`scale` custom data, and the scene-wide pass that calls it scales every
entity that does not carry `scalable = 0`. No antiportal carries one.
128 * 0.5 = 64, times the node's own scale. The remake invented 16 and the port
read it, so every no-portal field in the game was a QUARTER of its size. All 64
antiportal nodes across 45 levels carry a scale, from 1.3 to 13.
It is also why the ring looks wrong: the original draws the ring at 128 * scale,
so the circle you see IS the field. That half is not fixed here - the converter
writes no scale on the sprite, and the converter is the oracle for what is drawn.
_radius_note: THE REMAKE'S GUESS, KEPT ON PURPOSE. The decode above says 64, and it is not
applied, because one thing in the level data argues against it and nothing in
the files can settle which is right.
level6 carries antiportal_687 at (288, 192) with scale 3. At 64 its field would
cover x 96..480 of a level that spans x -64..576 - and the projectile blocker,
anti_projectile_wall_ent_743 at (313, 185), would sit entirely inside it. A wall
that stops a SHOT is pointless in a region where no portal may be placed anyway,
so either the radius is smaller than 64 x scale or that level is built oddly.
test_mp_shot's blocker case is the same point as data: with the blocker removed
its shot must land at (380, 150), which is 101 px from the field - outside at
Everything else checks out: the engine's GetSize is GetCurrentSize, that returns
frame x m_properties.scale, the ring is 128 with SpriteCut 1x1, the scene-wide
pass scales every entity that does not opt out, and no hd/ sprite path exists in
the whole decoded script - so the 64 is not a misreading of an HD asset.
This wants the owner playing the original: how big is the white ring on screen,
and can a portal be placed just outside the blocker in 1-7? Until then the port
keeps the remake's number and this file records the other one.
_not_modelled: A destroyed antiportal refuses nothing: isPointInAntiPortalField returns false
for an entity that is not IsAlive, and antiportal_explosion.ent exists. The port
has no notion of destroying one.
The original's test is strict - squaredDistance < r*r - where the port's is <=.
A tap exactly on the edge is refused by the port and allowed by the original.
